findings.title: To Catch a Ransomware Scammer, FBI Posed as Both Victim and Attacker
findings.summary_md: 404 Media, in collaboration with Court Watch, reported that federal prosecutors said the FBI posed as both a ransomware victim and a threat actor during an undercover operation against a Florida data recovery firm run by Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar and an unnamed associate. The company began in 2020 and claimed to offer data recovery services for ransomware victims. The article also describes legitimate victims listed in the indictment, including a Kansas business that Palacio allegedly charged $720,000.

findings.title: FBI posed as ransomware victim and attacker in sting on Florida recovery firm
findings.summary_md: RuntimeWire reported that Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar faces three wire fraud counts after prosecutors said his Florida firm charged $13,260 to recover files and paid $6,003 for the decryption key. The report says the FBI ran both sides of a ransomware incident to test a recovery firm that claimed it could restore encrypted files without paying attackers, with the undercover agent playing both the victim and the attacker demanding payment.

findings.title: FBI Played Hacker and Victim to Snare a Ransomware 'Rescuer'
findings.summary_md: Liberty Bell Report reported that Palacio faced three federal wire fraud counts and described an undercover agent posing as a Rhode Island ransomware victim while a second FBI employee played the gang. The report says the firm charged a $2,750 assessment and quoted $13,260, then paid about $6,003 in bitcoin for the key, and that a Kansas business was billed $720,000. It attributes the account to 404 Media and RuntimeWire and notes a parallel October case against the owner of MonsterCloud.
